podcast.body: Featured on *Pleasant Dreams*, this song was written by Joey Ramone. It is described as an "apparent diatribe against racism," but may have obliquely referred to a personal conflict between Joey and Johnny Ramone regarding a former girlfriend, Linda, whom Johnny later married. "On one track, the KKK took my baby away, written by Joey Ramone and apparent diatribe against racism."

podcast.body: This song, written by Joey Ramone, gained new context and meaning after the details of the love triangle involving Joey, Johnny Ramone, and Linda Danielle became known. It was written around the time his relationship issues with Linda were escalating. "Now that you know the story, this song from 1982 written by Joey just as the girlfriend issues were getting weird makes a whole lot more sense."

podcast.body: Though the Ramones were presented as a punk brotherhood, singer Joey and guitarist Johnny effectively stopped speaking after 1981 and communicated virtually not at all for over 20 years — through thousands of gigs and at least 12 albums. The rift had three dimensions: Johnny excluded Joey and Dee Dee from media interviews starting in 1978, believing they made the band look dumb; the two were polar political opposites (Johnny was a hardcore Republican who loved Reagan and both Bushes; Joey was a Democrat and anti-Reaganite); and most crucially, Johnny stole Joey's girlfriend Linda Danielle and married her. Joey never forgave him. "KKK Took My Baby Away" (1981) was Joey's coded strike against Johnny. The feud was never resolved: Joey died on April 15, 2001, and Johnny on September 17, 2004, with ill feeling still intact. "The singer and the guitarist, two of the founding members of one of the most important bands of all time, didn't speak to each other for 20 years through thousands of gigs and at least 12 albums."
